summary: ETH Zurich's Excellence Scholarship & Opportunity Programme (ESOP) pays CHF 13,500 per semester (from autumn 2027) plus a full tuition waiver for the standard length of an ETH master's. About 60 are awarded each year. Winners are top-10% bachelor's graduates who also show initiative beyond grades and can outline a credible master's thesis idea.
lookfor: A very good bachelor's result: top 10% of your class
A motivation letter that explains why you deserve an Excellence scholarship, including achievements beyond the classroom
A focused, feasible master's thesis pre-proposal (max 500 words) written by you
Two strong reference letters from professors
Performance in a phone/video interview (February) if shortlisted
cycle: For autumn 2027: apply in eApply between 1 and 30 November 2026 (the FAQ and dates page give 11:59 CET as the cut-off—treat it as midday and submit by 28 November); interviews February 2027; results end of March 2027.

eligibility.q: Are you in (or will you finish in) the top 10% of your bachelor's class?
eligibility.no: ESOP is out of reach; consider applying to ETH without ESOP and look at other Swiss or European awards (e.g. Radboud, Eiffel).

eligibility.q: Are you applying for a regular ETH master's (not an MAS) and do you NOT already hold or study for a master's?
eligibility.no: Holders of a master's and MAS applicants are excluded; consider PhD routes instead.

eligibility.q: Can you apply in the November 2026 window (the first application window)?
eligibility.no: ESOP is only open in the first window for international bachelor's holders. Mark 1 November 2027 for the next round.

eligibility.q: Do you meet your chosen programme's admission requirements and English requirement?
eligibility.no: Check the programme's specific requirements first; ESOP is only possible alongside a valid master's application.

eligibility.q: Can you pay the CHF 150 application fee by credit card (or PostFinance card)?
eligibility.no: The fee cannot be waived; arrange a dollar-enabled card or a sponsor's card early.

steps.title: Confirm you are top 10% and pick your ETH master's
steps.why: The scholarship is tied to one master's programme; the grant cannot be moved to another programme later.
do: Open the ESOP page and read the eligibility rules.
Ask your department or registrar for a letter stating your class position or that you are in the top 10% (e.g. by CGPA rank).
Browse ETH master's programmes and read the programme-specific requirements for your best fit.
Decide on one programme (each application costs CHF 150).
tips: A rank letter from your Head of Department makes 'top 10%' easy for selectors to verify when your grading scale is unfamiliar.
avoid: Applying to a programme your bachelor's does not prepare you for; you can be rejected for admission and lose ESOP with it.
check: I have proof of my class rank.
I know my programme's specific requirements.

steps.title: Plan your November around the 30th
steps.why: Late or incomplete applications are not processed, and the November window is short.
do: Write the dates down: window 1–30 Nov 2026; your own target 25 November.
Set reminders: 10 Oct rank letter; 20 Oct referees asked; 1 Nov eApply open; 15 Nov pre-proposal final.
Check that the language certificate (or English-medium confirmation) will be ready before you submit.
tips: The deadline time on the dates page is 11:59 (morning, CET). Do not wait for the evening of 30 November.
avoid: Thinking you have until 15 December; that was older guidance.
check: My target submission date is at least 3 days before 30 November.

steps.title: Open your eApply account and map the form
steps.why: Knowing every tab early stops last-minute surprises (e.g. referee emails, consent form).
do: Go to eApply and create an account on 1 November when the window opens.
Choose your master's programme and indicate that you are applying for ESOP.
List what each tab asks for: personal data, education history, documents, references, payment.
Download the Declaration of Consent form, sign it and scan it.
tips: Enter your education history exactly as your transcripts show it.
avoid: Leaving the payment step to the last day; card failures are common.
check: I can log in and I know which uploads are still missing.

steps.title: Collect official transcripts and certificates
steps.why: Admissions screens your documents before the committee sees your ESOP file.
do: Request official transcripts from every university you attended, issued by the Registrar/Exams and Records, showing courses, grades, credits and the grading system.
If you are still studying, get an enrolment confirmation with your expected degree title and date.
Scan your degree certificate (a provisional certificate or statement of result is accepted if the final one is not issued).
Scan your secondary-school certificate (e.g. WAEC/NECO) and passport photo page.
tips: Ask the registrar to include the grading scale on the transcript; it helps reviewers judge your top-10% claim.
avoid: Uploading an unofficial student-portal printout as your transcript (only ETH's own students may do that).
check: Every university I attended has an official transcript scanned.

steps.title: Sort out English: test or English-medium confirmation
steps.why: A missing or insufficient language certificate means rejection on formal grounds, without review.
do: Check if your bachelor's was taught in English. If yes, ask your university for an official letter confirming English as the language of instruction.
If not exempt, book TOEFL (institution code 9038), IELTS, or Cambridge C1/C2 well before November.
Check your programme page for the minimum score.
Make sure the certificate is not older than two years (C2 or C1 grade A: five years).
tips: Nigerian and Ghanaian degrees are usually taught in English, but ETH still needs the official confirmation letter.
avoid: Assuming the exemption is automatic; only UK, US, Ireland, Australia and NZ degrees skip the letter.
check: I have a valid certificate or an official English-medium letter ready to upload.

steps.title: Write a detailed chronological CV
steps.why: ETH asks for a continuous record from secondary school to now; gaps raise questions.
do: List education and work month by month from secondary school to today with no unexplained gaps (include NYSC if applicable).
Give full detail on your academic history: degree, institution, CGPA, rank, thesis title.
Add research, publications, awards, competitions, leadership and volunteering.
Write it in English (the language of your programme).
tips: Extracurricular achievements matter for ESOP; give each one a result.

steps.title: Draft the master's thesis pre-proposal
steps.why: Only ESOP applicants write this; it shows you can think like a researcher within the master's timeframe.
do: Read the official pre-proposal guidelines PDF.
Browse your programme's research groups and pick a topic close to one of them.
Use these headings: Title; Introduction; Objectives and goals; Methods; Background/prior work (include your own); Timetable and milestones (4–6 months); References.
Keep the text to 500 words or fewer, excluding references.
Cite every source; the text must be your own work (plagiarism disqualifies you).
tips: Narrow is better: one question you could answer in a 6-month thesis.
Link your methods to skills shown in your CV or bachelor's project.
avoid: Copying text from a professor's webpage or paper.
check: A professor in that group could see it is feasible.

links.t: Watch: The Pre-Proposal that got me the ESOP (Excellence Scholarship at ETH Zurich) (David Alonso)

steps.prompt: Master's thesis pre-proposal: title, introduction, objectives, methods, prior work, timetable, references.

steps.title: Write the ESOP motivation letter
steps.why: ETH says the ESOP letter must go further than the programme letter and explain why you deserve an Excellence scholarship.
do: Check the ESOP upload in eApply for any length rule; if none is stated, keep to 1–2 pages.
Open with the specific scientific interest that brings you to this ETH programme.
Give evidence of excellence: rank, prizes, research, competitions.
Add achievements beyond the classroom: leadership, teaching, community or start-up work.
Explain how ETH (named labs, courses) fits your plan and what you will do afterwards.
End with why the scholarship matters for you.
tips: Every claim should have proof elsewhere in your file (CV, rank letter, references).
avoid: Re-using your programme motivation letter unchanged.
Focusing mainly on financial need; ESOP is merit-based.
check: The letter answers 'why me for an Excellence scholarship?' in the first half page.
steps.prompt: Explain in more detail why you deserve an Excellence scholarship, including extracurricular achievements.
steps.limit: Check the current guidance (1–2 pages is common)

steps.title: Line up two professors as referees
steps.why: Referees upload their letters themselves after you submit, so they must be ready to act fast in late November or December.
do: Choose two professors/lecturers who know your work well (if you work in industry: one academic plus one employer).
In October, email them your CV, pre-proposal draft and a note on the programme.
Get each referee's official institutional email address—eApply does not accept Gmail, Yahoo or Hotmail.
Enter their details in the eApply References tab.
After you submit, ETH emails them; reminders go out after 10 days. Follow up politely if they have not uploaded.
tips: Many Nigerian lecturers use Gmail; ask early whether they have a working university email.
avoid: Entering a personal email—the referee may never get the request.
check: Both referees agreed and gave me an official email.

steps.title: Upload, pay CHF 150 and submit
steps.why: The application is final only when the fee is paid and you get the confirmation email.
do: Upload: transcripts, certificates, secondary-school certificate, passport, CV, language proof, signed consent form, programme-specific documents.
Upload ESOP items: motivation letter, pre-proposal, CV, referee details.
Proofread every PDF and file name.
Pay CHF 150 by credit card or PostFinance card.
Submit and save the confirmation email.
tips: Submit 3–5 days early so card or upload problems can be fixed.
avoid: Late or incomplete applications are not processed.

links.t: Watch: ETH Master's Application Explained (Tutorial) (Thomas - Oxford)

steps.title: Prepare for the February interview
steps.why: Shortlisted ESOP candidates have phone or video interviews in February 2027.
do: Re-read your pre-proposal and be ready to explain the method and timeline in 2 minutes.
Prepare answers on: why ETH, why this programme, your best achievement, your plan after the master's.
Test your internet, camera and a quiet room; have a backup (mobile data).
Do one mock interview with a lecturer or past scholar.
tips: Expect technical questions on your field; revise core bachelor's topics.
avoid: Reading answers from notes on screen.
check: I can explain my pre-proposal clearly without notes.

steps.title: Get results and prepare for Zurich
steps.why: Decisions come at the end of March; Swiss visa and banking take time.
do: Check eApply for your admission decision and the ESOP result (end of March).
If successful, accept the offer and start your Swiss student visa application at the Swiss embassy (check the embassy's processing time).
Open a Swiss bank or postal account after arrival; ESOP is paid in instalments at the start of each semester into a Swiss account.
If not nominated, you can still take the admission offer if you can fund it—ESOP outcome does not affect admission.
tips: Compulsory long internships can pause payments; read the FAQ before planning one.
avoid: Assuming payments start before you arrive and enrol.
check: I know my result and next deadline.

faq.a: CHF 13,500 per semester from autumn 2027, plus a tuition fee waiver, for the standard length of the master's (3–4 semesters).

faq.q: Is there a separate ESOP portal?
faq.a: No. You apply in eApply together with your master's application in the November window.

faq.q: If I do not get ESOP, am I rejected for the master's?
faq.a: No. ETH states that not receiving an ESOP nomination does not affect admission.

faq.q: Do I need a supervisor before writing the pre-proposal?
faq.a: No. It is an outline that will change with your supervisor later, but it should match the research in your programme.

faq.q: Can my referee send the letter by email?
faq.a: No. ETH emails your referee after you submit and they upload it themselves.
